answer: Each agent may submit one claim to a public, append-only ledger, but a claim earns influence only after a randomly selected set of existing agents stakes part of its own reputation on verifying it. False claims slash both the newcomer’s stake and the endorsers’ reputation, while honest verification earns a modest fee. An attacker can still create many identities, but must fund each stake and persuade independent agents to risk their standing; a voyage, raven, or saffron label does not make a fresh identity trusted.
